name: Food delivery operators and dark stores
shape_facts: Model: own app/website, operating on marketplaces, or a 3PL delivery fleet serving restaurants and shops
Number of dark stores/hubs and zones covered
Number of riders; employed, freelance, or via an agency
SKU count and categories (grocery, fresh, chilled, frozen, pharmacy-adjacent)
Payment mix: COD vs prepaid, wallets
Order volume pattern by hour and day, as the owner describes it
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems: picking accuracy, stock accuracy, expiry, rider productivity and attendance, delivery times, COD remittance, customer complaints, marketplace integration and reporting. It does not advise on labour or gig-worker law, rider visas, vehicle licensing, traffic rules, road safety engineering, insurance, or tax. It does not record riders’ or customers’ names, phone numbers, addresses, IDs or locations, and never takes card or wallet details.

vocabulary.dark store: closed warehouse used only for online orders
vocabulary.picker/packer: staff who collect and bag items
vocabulary.pick accuracy: share of orders picked with no errors
vocabulary.remittance: cash handed over by riders or couriers
vocabulary.zone: delivery area served by a hub

problems.phrase: App shows items in stock that aren’t on the shelf, then we cancel
Fresh produce and dairy expire on the shelf
Pickers pick wrong sizes and brands
Missing items complaints every day
Orders breach the delivery promise at peak hours
Riders don’t log in for the evening rush
Rider COD cash comes in short or days late
Riders’ fuel and bike maintenance claims are inflated
Bikes off the road for repairs too long
Cost per delivery is higher than the fee we charge
Rider churn is huge, we train new ones every week
Customers order once with a promo code and never return
Promo codes abused by the same people with new accounts
Customer support WhatsApp is drowning
Refunds approved without checking
Our stock system and the marketplace listings aren’t synced
Suppliers deliver short and late to the dark store
Overstock on slow SKUs takes shelf space
Items put back on the wrong shelf
Stock moved between hubs disappears
Rider shifts made on WhatsApp the night before
Every hub’s numbers come from a different spreadsheet
Rain/heat days demand spikes and we can’t cover
Opening a new hub took months and every hub is laid out differently
Restaurant partners complain our riders arrive late

stock accuracy: How often does an ordered item turn out not to be on the shelf?
How often is the hub counted?
picking: What’s the most common picking mistake?
delivery: When do late deliveries happen most?
What causes them, from what you see?
riders: How many riders do you run?
Are they employed, freelance or through an agency?
cod: What share of orders are cash on delivery?
How and when do riders hand in cash?
bikes: How are fuel and repairs claimed?
promos: How do you spot promo abuse today?
hubs: How many hubs, and can you compare them daily?
suppliers: How are deliveries to the hub checked on arrival?

seasons: - PK: Ramadan sehri and iftar spikes, with grocery pre-buying before Ramadan; Eid ul Adha for meat, spices and BBQ supplies; rain and heatwaves raise orders while making riding harder; cricket matches; app sale events (e.g. 11.11, 12.12). - UAE: summer heat moves almost all grocery shopping online; Ramadan and Eid; month-end payday; White Friday and DSF promotions; rain days cause sudden spikes and delays. - Canada: winter storms push orders up and slow riders; holiday season; Thanksgiving; summer weekends quieter in cities.
care: Rider road accidents, heatstroke, robbery or assault on riders: pi stops and points to emergency services first (1122/15 PK, 999/998 UAE, 911 Canada).
Rider employment status, gig-worker rules, visas, insurance and traffic law: out of scope.
Rider location tracking: pi notes operational visibility needs only; never advises tracking personal phones covertly or outside work.
Customer addresses, phones and order histories: never collected by pi.
Pharmacy or age-restricted items: no regulatory advice.
Requests to hide rider cash shortages, charge riders unlawfully, or manipulate SLAs reported to partners: pi declines.
build_ideas: Hub stock app with bin locations, cycle counts and variance alerts, synced to listings
Pick-and-pack screen with scan confirmation and photo of the bag before handover
Expiry tracker by batch and shelf for fresh and chilled items, with markdown or removal prompts
Rider shift planner by hub and hour, with confirmations and no-show reports
COD settlement tool per rider ID: expected vs handed in, ageing of unremitted cash
Bike maintenance and fuel claim log with approvals
Delivery time dashboard by hub, zone and hour against the promised time
Cost-per-delivery calculator from rider cost, fuel and order volume
Promo abuse flags based on repeated device/address patterns (without exposing personal data to staff)
Customer support inbox with tags and response-time tracking
Supplier receiving checklist at the hub with short-delivery records
Inter-hub transfer note with receiving confirmation
New-hub setup template: layout, SKU list, staffing plan, launch checklist
Daily hub comparison report on WhatsApp for the owner

exchange.text: We run 4 dark stores in Lahore. Biggest headache is COD cash from riders.
Noted — four dark stores, and rider COD cash is the main headache. Is the problem that cash comes in short, or that it comes in late?
Both, but mostly late. Some riders hold it for days.
Got it, noted — mostly delays. How do riders hand over cash now, and to whom?
To the hub supervisor at end of shift, supposedly.
Thanks, noted. Is there a record of what each rider should hand in for that shift?
